c.tagline: India's Pink City, a royal Rajput capital of forts, bazaars, and rose-hued facades.

taxi.color: Radio cabs are unbranded; auto-rickshaws are green & yellow
taxi.fareNote: Auto-rickshaws rarely use the meter—agree a flat fare before boarding. App cabs (Uber/Ola) and bike/auto app Rapido are metered and the simplest way to avoid haggling.

emergency.note: 112 is India's unified emergency number; 100 reaches police, 108 ambulance, and 101 fire directly.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Aggressive touts and commission scams at the forts; gem-export and "government emporium" scams

hood_desc: The walled historic core painted terracotta-pink, home to the City Palace, Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar, and the buzzing bazaars of Johari and Bapu; best for first-timers who want the landmarks and markets on their doorstep.

Jaipur's upscale, leafy modern quarter around Statue Circle and Ashok Marg, packed with fine-dining restaurants, cafes, bars, and boutiques; suits travelers who want a cosmopolitan base with the city's best nightlife and dining.

A calm, green residential neighborhood of heritage guesthouses and boutique hotels, walkable to the railway station and Sindhi Camp bus stand; ideal for a peaceful, well-connected base close to the sights.
A quiet, orderly area of tree-lined avenues, government bungalows, and embassies west of the old city; good for a relaxed, upscale stay away from the crowds, with the metro and MI Road nearby.
Jaipur's main commercial artery linking the old city to the new, lined with shops, showrooms, banks, restaurants, and famous sweet shops; a convenient, central base for shopping and eating.
lodging: Umaid Bhawan - A Heritage Style Boutique Hotel

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only; avoid ice of unknown origin.

transit.pay: Buy a rechargeable metro Smart Card at any station counter for about ₹100 (~$1, including a ₹50 refundable deposit) for a 10% fare discount, or pay per ride with a token/QR ticket; single fares run ₹10-30 (~$0.10-0.30). JCTSL city buses take cash to the conductor (₹10-25); there is no unified city-wide transit card as of 2026.
transit.hours: The metro Pink Line runs roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM with trains every 10-15 minutes; city buses run from about 6:00 AM to 9:30 PM.
transit.note: The metro is a single Pink Line (Mansarovar to Badi Chaupar) mainly useful along that corridor, so most getting-around is by auto-rickshaw, app cabs (Uber/Ola), the Rapido bike/auto app, and JCTSL buses.

transit.m: Prepaid taxi or Uber/Ola to the Pink City (20-30 min)
Auto-rickshaw to central Jaipur / MI Road (~25-30 min)
JCTSL city bus toward Ajmeri Gate / MI Road area

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~5-10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated. Many upscale places already add a service charge, so check the bill first.
